records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, saying,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses. He said,

L.1: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying,

decisions.choice: a new speech: the rite for a person whose disease has healed
decisions.reason: Chapter 13 told the priest how to rule on a mark of scale disease (13:2-3). This speech, which runs to verse 32, tells what happens once the disease has gone: how the person is cleansed and brought back into the camp and to the sanctuary.

records.heading: Cleansing from serious skin disease

records.source: זֹ֤את תִּֽהְיֶה֙ תּוֹרַ֣ת הַמְּצֹרָ֔ע בְּי֖וֹם טָהֳרָת֑וֹ וְהוּבָ֖א אֶל־הַכֹּהֵֽן׃
records.gloss: This will be [the] law of the [one with] scale disease on [the] day of his cleansing: and he will be brought to the priest.
pieces: "This is the law for a person with a serious skin disease, for the day they are to be made clean. They are to be brought to the priest.

L.2: "This will be the law of the one with scale disease on the day of his cleansing: he will be brought to the priest.

R.2: "Here are the rules for the day when a person who had a serious skin disease is made clean. Someone must bring word of it to the priest.

decisions.choice: law: instruction, the set procedure for a case
decisions.reason: The word means teaching or instruction. In Leviticus it names the rule for one kind of offering or case: "the law of the burnt offering" (6:2), "the law of the mark" (13:59). Verses 32, 54 and 57 close the chapter with the same word.

decisions.choice: the one with scale disease: a person found to have it under chapter 13
decisions.reason: This is the person the priest pronounced unclean under 13:3 and who has lived outside the camp (13:45-46). On the disease itself, see 13:2.

decisions.choice: he will be brought: his case is brought before the priest
alternatives: he is led into the priest's presence
decisions.reason: The person cannot yet enter the camp, and verse 3 has the priest go out to him. So "he will be brought" most likely means that he is reported to the priest, or brought as far as the priest at the edge of the camp, as in 13:2.

decisions.choice: bring word of it to the priest
decisions.reason: Readable says that the priest is told, since the priest then goes out to the person (verse 3). Balanced keeps "brought to the priest".

records.source: וְיָצָא֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן אֶל־מִח֖וּץ לַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה וְרָאָה֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְהִנֵּ֛ה נִרְפָּ֥א נֶֽגַע־הַצָּרַ֖עַת מִן־הַצָּרֽוּעַ׃
records.gloss: And will go out the priest to outside the camp, and will see the priest, and there! has been healed [the] mark of the scale disease from the [one with] scale disease,
pieces: The priest is to go out of the camp and look the person over. If the sore of the serious skin disease has healed,

L.3: And the priest will go out to [the] outside of the camp, and the priest will look, and there! the mark of scale disease has been healed from the one with scale disease,

R.3: The priest must go outside the camp to check the person. He may find that the serious skin disease has gone away.

decisions.choice: the priest goes out: the person still lives outside the camp
decisions.reason: Someone with scale disease had to live alone outside the camp (13:46). The priest goes to them; they come in only after the first stage of cleansing (verse 8).

decisions.choice: has been healed: the healing comes first, the rite follows
decisions.reason: The priest does not heal. He checks that healing has already happened, and the rite then makes the person clean and restores them to the people and to worship. The verb is passive and names no healer; in Scripture healing belongs to God (Exodus 15:26).

decisions.choice: sore / serious skin disease
decisions.reason: The mark is a "sore" at Balanced, as in 13:2. Readable says only that the disease has gone.

records.source: וְצִוָּה֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְלָקַ֧ח לַמִּטַּהֵ֛ר שְׁתֵּֽי־צִפֳּרִ֥ים חַיּ֖וֹת טְהֹר֑וֹת וְעֵ֣ץ אֶ֔רֶז וּשְׁנִ֥י תוֹלַ֖עַת וְאֵזֹֽב׃
records.gloss: and will command the priest, and one will take for the [one] cleansing himself two birds living clean, and wood of cedar and scarlet of worm and hyssop.
pieces: the priest is to have someone take, for the one being cleansed, two clean birds that are alive, with some cedar wood, scarlet yarn and hyssop.

L.4: then the priest will command, and [someone] will take for the one being cleansed two living, clean birds, and cedar wood and scarlet yarn and hyssop.

R.4: Then the priest must tell someone to get two live birds of a clean kind for the person. They must also get some cedar wood, some red yarn and a hyssop plant.

decisions.choice: two living clean birds: wild birds of a kind Israel may eat
decisions.reason: The general word for a small bird is used, not the doves of verse 22. "Clean" means a kind not forbidden as food (11:13-19). "Living" matters because one bird is killed and the other is set free alive (verses 5-7).

decisions.choice: cedar wood, scarlet yarn and hyssop: the same three things as in the rite of Numbers 19
alternatives: cedar: perhaps a juniper; hyssop: perhaps a kind of marjoram
decisions.reason: Cedar is a lasting, fragrant wood. "Scarlet of worm" is wool or thread dyed crimson with a dye made from an insect. Hyssop is a small, leafy plant used to sprinkle liquid (Exodus 12:22; Psalm 51:9). The three appear together again in verses 49-52 and in the burning of the red cow for the water of cleansing (Numbers 19:6). The text does not say what each stands for, and the reading of them as life, blood or cleansing is an inference; verse 6 shows the hyssop and cedar bound up with the living bird and dipped together.

decisions.choice: someone will take: the priest gives the order, another person fetches
decisions.reason: The verb "take" has no stated subject after "the priest will command". The priest's part is to direct the rite; someone else, perhaps the person being cleansed, supplies the birds and the rest.

decisions.choice: scarlet yarn / red yarn
decisions.reason: "Scarlet of worm" names the color and the source of the dye, not the material, but it was dyed wool or thread (Exodus 25:4). Readable says "red yarn". Literal keeps "the one being cleansed" for the person who is purifying himself; the verb form means one who is undergoing cleansing.

records.source: וְצִוָּה֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְשָׁחַ֖ט אֶת־הַצִּפּ֣וֹר הָאֶחָ֑ת אֶל־כְּלִי־חֶ֖רֶשׂ עַל־מַ֥יִם חַיִּֽים׃
records.gloss: And will command the priest, and one will slaughter the bird the one into a vessel of earthenware over water living.
pieces: At the priest's order one of the birds is to be slaughtered over fresh water held in a clay pot.

L.5: And the priest will command, and [someone] will slaughter the one bird into an earthenware vessel over living water.

R.5: The priest must tell someone to kill one of the birds. Its blood must drain into a clay pot that has fresh water in it.

decisions.choice: living water: fresh water from a spring or stream
decisions.reason: "Living" water is water that flows, not water stored in a cistern (Genesis 26:19; Jeremiah 2:13). It is used again in verses 6, 50-52 and in 15:13.

decisions.choice: into a clay pot over the water: the blood runs into the water
decisions.reason: The bird is killed over the pot so that its blood mixes with the water in it, and the living bird and the other things are dipped in that mixture (verse 6). A clay pot that becomes unclean is broken, not washed (6:21; 11:33).

decisions.choice: Its blood must drain into
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what killing the bird "into" the pot means.

records.source: אֶת־הַצִּפֹּ֤ר הַֽחַיָּה֙ יִקַּ֣ח אֹתָ֔הּ וְאֶת־עֵ֥ץ הָאֶ֛רֶז וְאֶת־שְׁנִ֥י הַתּוֹלַ֖עַת וְאֶת־הָאֵזֹ֑ב וְטָבַ֨ל אוֹתָ֜ם וְאֵ֣ת׀הַצִּפֹּ֣ר הַֽחַיָּ֗ה בְּדַם֙ הַצִּפֹּ֣ר הַשְּׁחֻטָ֔ה עַ֖ל הַמַּ֥יִם הַֽחַיִּֽים׃
records.gloss: The bird the living he will take it, and the wood of the cedar and the scarlet of the worm and the hyssop, and he will dip them and the bird the living in [the] blood of the bird the slaughtered over the water the living.
pieces: Then he is to take the live bird and the cedar wood, the scarlet yarn and the hyssop, and dip them all, live bird too, into the blood of the bird that was killed over the fresh water.

L.6: The living bird he will take, and the cedar wood and the scarlet yarn and the hyssop, and he will dip them and the living bird in the blood of the bird that was slaughtered over the living water.

R.6: Then the priest must take the live bird, the cedar wood, the red yarn and the hyssop. He must dip all of them into the blood of the dead bird, which is mixed with the fresh water.

decisions.choice: the living bird first: the stress falls on the bird that will go free
decisions.reason: The sentence puts the living bird before its verb, and names it again after the dipping. Everything is dipped together; the hyssop, perhaps tied to the cedar with the yarn, can then be used to sprinkle.

decisions.choice: the blood ... over the living water: the blood mixed with the water in the pot
decisions.reason: "Over the living water" repeats verse 5: the bird was killed above the water. Verse 51 names both, "the blood of the slaughtered bird and the living water".

records.source: וְהִזָּ֗ה עַ֧ל הַמִּטַּהֵ֛ר מִן־הַצָּרַ֖עַת שֶׁ֣בַע פְּעָמִ֑ים וְטִ֣הֲר֔וֹ וְשִׁלַּ֛ח אֶת־הַצִּפֹּ֥ר הַֽחַיָּ֖ה עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הַשָּׂדֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And he will sprinkle on the [one] cleansing himself from the scale disease seven times, and he will pronounce him clean, and he will send off the bird the living over [the] face of the field.
pieces: He is to sprinkle the one being cleansed from the serious skin disease seven times and declare them clean. Then he is to set the live bird free in the open country.

L.7: And he will sprinkle on the one being cleansed from the scale disease seven times, and he will pronounce him clean, and he will let the living bird go over the face of the field.

R.7: He must sprinkle the person seven times with the blood and water. Then he must say that the person is clean. After that he must let the live bird fly away into the open fields.

decisions.choice: sprinkle seven times: a full, complete sprinkling
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for sprinkling blood before the veil (4:6), not the splashing against the altar (1:5). Seven marks completeness, as in 4:6 and 16:14.

decisions.choice: pronounce him clean: the first stage of cleansing
decisions.reason: The priest's ruling here lets the person return to the camp (verse 8). Full cleansing comes in stages: after washing (verse 8), after a second washing on the seventh day (verse 9), and after the offerings on the eighth (verse 20). On the priest's ruling see 13:3.

decisions.choice: the living bird set free: the uncleanness is sent away
decisions.reason: The text does not explain the rite. The bird, dipped in the blood of the other, flies off into open country, away from the camp, as the goat for Azazel is sent into the wilderness carrying the people's sins (16:21-22). The same is done for a house in verse 53.

decisions.choice: with the blood and water
decisions.reason: Readable names what is sprinkled, from verse 6.

records.source: וְכִבֶּס֩ הַמִּטַּהֵ֨ר אֶת־בְּגָדָ֜יו וְגִלַּ֣ח אֶת־כָּל־שְׂעָר֗וֹ וְרָחַ֤ץ בַּמַּ֨יִם֙ וְטָהֵ֔ר וְאַחַ֖ר יָב֣וֹא אֶל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה וְיָשַׁ֛ב מִח֥וּץ לְאָהֳל֖וֹ שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִֽים׃
records.gloss: And will wash the [one] cleansing himself his garments, and he will shave all his hair, and he will bathe in water, and he will be clean; and after he will come into the camp, and he will stay outside his tent seven days.
pieces: Then the one being cleansed is to wash their clothes, shave off all their hair, and bathe in water, and so become clean. After that they may enter the camp, but for seven days they are to live outside their own tent.

L.8: And the one being cleansed will wash his garments and shave all his hair and bathe in water, and he will be clean; and after [that] he will come into the camp, but he will stay outside his tent seven days.

R.8: Next the person must wash their clothes and shave off all their hair. Then they must take a bath. When they do these things, they will be clean. They may come back into the camp. But for seven days they must stay outside their own tent.

decisions.choice: he will be clean: clean enough to enter the camp
decisions.reason: This is a stage of cleanness, not the last one. The person may come back among the people but not yet into their own tent, and must wash again on the seventh day (verse 9) and bring offerings on the eighth (verse 10).

decisions.choice: outside his tent: back in the camp, but not yet at home
decisions.reason: The person lives near home but not in it for a week. The text gives no reason; it may keep any remaining uncleanness away from the household and their belongings (compare verse 36, where things are carried out of a house before it can make them unclean).

decisions.choice: the one being cleansed / they
decisions.reason: The law covers men and women alike, so Balanced and Readable use "they" for the person. Literal keeps "he" and "his", as the Hebrew has them.

records.source: וְהָיָה֩ בַיּ֨וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֜י יְגַלַּ֣ח אֶת־כָּל־שְׂעָר֗וֹ אֶת־רֹאשׁ֤וֹ וְאֶת־זְקָנוֹ֙ וְאֵת֙ גַּבֹּ֣ת עֵינָ֔יו וְאֶת־כָּל־שְׂעָר֖וֹ יְגַלֵּ֑חַ וְכִבֶּ֣ס אֶת־בְּגָדָ֗יו וְרָחַ֧ץ אֶת־בְּשָׂר֛וֹ בַּמַּ֖יִם וְטָהֵֽר׃
records.gloss: And it will be on the day the seventh he will shave all his hair: his head and his beard and [the] eyebrows of his eyes, and all his hair he will shave; and he will wash his garments and he will bathe his body in water, and he will be clean.
pieces: On the seventh day they are to shave again, all of it: the hair of the head, the beard, the eyebrows, every hair on the body. They are to wash their clothes and bathe their body in water, and they will be clean.

L.9: And it will be on the seventh day [that] he will shave all his hair: his head and his beard and his eyebrows, all his hair he will shave; and he will wash his garments and bathe his body in water, and he will be clean.

R.9: On the seventh day they must shave again. They must shave the hair on their head, their beard, their eyebrows and every other hair. They must wash their clothes and bathe. Then they will be clean.

decisions.choice: all his hair ... he will shave: the shaving is total
decisions.reason: The verse says "shave" twice and "all his hair" twice around the list of head, beard and eyebrows. Nothing is to be left where the disease might hide; compare the hair as a sign of the disease in 13:3-4.

decisions.choice: he will be clean: the second stage, ready for the offerings
decisions.reason: After this washing the person may come to the entrance of the tent of meeting on the eighth day (verses 10-11).

records.source: וּבַיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁמִינִ֗י יִקַּ֤ח שְׁנֵֽי־כְבָשִׂים֙ תְּמִימִ֔ים וְכַבְשָׂ֥ה אַחַ֛ת בַּת־שְׁנָתָ֖הּ תְּמִימָ֑ה וּשְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה עֶשְׂרֹנִ֗ים סֹ֤לֶת מִנְחָה֙ בְּלוּלָ֣ה בַשֶּׁ֔מֶן וְלֹ֥ג אֶחָ֖ד שָֽׁמֶן׃
records.gloss: And on the day the eighth he will take two male lambs unblemished and ewe-lamb one, a daughter of her year, unblemished, and three tenths of fine flour [as] a grain offering mixed with oil, and log one of oil.
pieces: On the eighth day they are to take two male lambs without defect and one year-old ewe lamb without defect, with {{units:about 6 quarts|three tenths of an ephah}} of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering, and {{units:about a third of a quart|a log}} of oil.

L.10: And on the eighth day he will take two unblemished male lambs and one unblemished ewe lamb, a year old, and three tenths [of an ephah] of fine flour [as] a grain offering mixed with oil, and one log of oil.

R.10: On the eighth day they must bring two male lambs and one female lamb a year old. The animals must be healthy and perfect. They must also bring {{units:about 6 quarts|three tenths of an ephah}} of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering, and {{units:about a third of a quart|a log}} of olive oil.

decisions.choice: three tenths: three tenths of an ephah, about six quarts of flour
decisions.reason: The ephah is not named, but "tenths" are tenths of an ephah, as in Numbers 28:12-13, where a tenth goes with each lamb. An ephah was a dry measure of about twenty quarts, so a tenth was about two quarts (5:11) and three tenths about six. The three tenths here match the three animals; the poor person brings one tenth with one lamb (verse 21).

decisions.choice: a log: a small liquid measure, about a third of a quart
decisions.reason: The log appears only in this chapter (verses 10, 12, 15, 21, 24). Later Jewish reckoning made it a twelfth of a hin, which gives about a third of a quart; the exact size in Moses' day is not known. This oil is separate from the oil in the flour: it is waved before the LORD and then put on the person (verses 12-18).

decisions.choice: two male lambs and a ewe lamb: guilt, sin and burnt offerings
decisions.reason: Verses 12-20 assign them: one male lamb for the guilt offering, the ewe lamb for the sin offering (a female, as for a common person in 4:32), and the other male lamb for the burnt offering. On "unblemished" see 1:3.

decisions.choice: about 6 quarts / about a third of a quart
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give modern measures, with the ephah and the log as the Measures setting. Literal keeps "three tenths [of an ephah]" and "log".

decisions.choice: olive oil
decisions.reason: The oil of Israel's offerings was olive oil (Exodus 27:20); Readable says so.

records.source: וְהֶעֱמִ֞יד הַכֹּהֵ֣ן הַֽמְטַהֵ֗ר אֵ֛ת הָאִ֥ישׁ הַמִּטַּהֵ֖ר וְאֹתָ֑ם לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה פֶּ֖תַח אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃
records.gloss: And will station the priest who cleanses the man who is cleansing himself and them before Yahweh, [at the] entrance of [the] tent of meeting.
pieces: The priest who is declaring them clean is to set {{gender:the person|the man}} being cleansed, and these offerings, before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at the entrance of the tent of meeting.

L.11: And the priest who pronounces [him] clean will station {{gender:the person|the man}} being cleansed, and them, before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, [at the] entrance of the tent of meeting.

R.11: The priest who says that the person is clean must have them stand before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at the entrance of the meeting tent. Their offerings must be there too.

decisions.choice: at the entrance of the tent of meeting: as near as a lay worshiper comes
decisions.reason: The person, once shut out of the camp, now stands at the very door of God's tent, where offerings are brought (1:3). On the tent of meeting see 1:1.

decisions.choice: the priest who pronounces clean: the priest in charge of this person's case
decisions.reason: The verb form is the one in verse 7, "he will pronounce him clean". The same priest who ruled on the person carries out the whole rite.

records.source: וְלָקַ֨ח הַכֹּהֵ֜ן אֶת־הַכֶּ֣בֶשׂ הָאֶחָ֗ד וְהִקְרִ֥יב אֹת֛וֹ לְאָשָׁ֖ם וְאֶת־לֹ֣ג הַשָּׁ֑מֶן וְהֵנִ֥יף אֹתָ֛ם תְּנוּפָ֖ה לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And will take the priest the male lamb the one, and he will bring it near for a guilt offering, and the log of the oil, and he will wave them [as] a wave offering before Yahweh.
pieces: The priest is to take one of the male lambs and present it as a guilt offering, together with the log of oil, and lift them up and wave them as a wave offering before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.12: And the priest will take the one male lamb and bring it near for a guilt offering, with the log of oil, and he will wave them [as] a wave offering before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.12: The priest must take one of the male lambs and offer it as a guilt offering. He must take the oil too. He must lift up both of them before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as a wave offering.

decisions.choice: a guilt offering: an offering that pays back what was owed
decisions.reason: The guilt offering is brought where something due to God or a neighbor has been lost or held back (5:15; see the note there). The text does not say what was lost here. One reading is that the person, shut out of the sanctuary for so long, could bring no offerings while unclean; another, that the disease was taken as a sign of a wrong against what is holy (Numbers 12:10; 2 Chronicles 26:16-21).

decisions.choice: wave them as a wave offering: lift them up and present them before the LORD
decisions.reason: A wave offering was held up and moved before the LORD to show that it was given to him and then handed back to the priest (7:30; 8:27). Usually only part of an animal is waved; here the whole living lamb and the oil are, as the Levites are "waved" in Numbers 8:11.

decisions.choice: lift them up and wave them
decisions.reason: Balanced spells out the action. Literal keeps "wave them [as] a wave offering", the Hebrew's verb and its noun.

records.source: וְשָׁחַ֣ט אֶת־הַכֶּ֗בֶשׂ בִּ֠מְקוֹם אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִשְׁחַ֧ט אֶת־הַֽחַטָּ֛את וְאֶת־הָעֹלָ֖ה בִּמְק֣וֹם הַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ כִּ֡י כַּ֠חַטָּאת הָאָשָׁ֥ם הוּא֙ לַכֹּהֵ֔ן קֹ֥דֶשׁ קָֽדָשִׁ֖ים הֽוּא׃
records.gloss: And he will slaughter the male lamb in [the] place where one slaughters the sin offering and the burnt offering, in [the] place of the holiness; for like the sin offering the guilt offering, it [belongs] to the priest; most holy it [is].
pieces: He is to slaughter the lamb at the place in the holy area where the sin offering and the burnt offering are slaughtered. The guilt offering goes to the priest, just as the sin offering does; it is most holy.

L.13: And he will slaughter the male lamb in the place where they slaughter the sin offering and the burnt offering, in the holy place; for like the sin offering, the guilt offering [belongs] to the priest; it [is] a most holy [thing].

R.13: He must kill the lamb in the holy area, at the place where the sin offerings and the burnt offerings are killed. The guilt offering belongs to the priest, the same as the sin offering. It is very holy.

decisions.choice: the place where the sin offering and burnt offering are slaughtered: on the north side of the altar
decisions.reason: Burnt offerings, sin offerings and guilt offerings are all slaughtered on the north side of the altar (1:11; 6:18; 7:2). This "holy place" is the court of the tent, not the inner room of 16:2.

decisions.choice: like the sin offering, the guilt offering belongs to the priest
decisions.reason: The meat of these offerings, once the fat is burned, is the priests' portion, eaten in a holy place by the priests alone (6:19, 22; 7:6-7).

decisions.choice: most holy: belonging wholly to God and his priests
decisions.reason: On "most holy" see 2:3; the guilt offering is called most holy in 7:1 and 7:6.

records.source: וְלָקַ֣ח הַכֹּהֵן֮ מִדַּ֣ם הָאָשָׁם֒ וְנָתַן֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן עַל־תְּנ֛וּךְ אֹ֥זֶן הַמִּטַּהֵ֖ר הַיְמָנִ֑ית וְעַל־בֹּ֤הֶן יָדוֹ֙ הַיְמָנִ֔ית וְעַל־בֹּ֥הֶן רַגְל֖וֹ הַיְמָנִֽית׃
records.gloss: And will take the priest from [the] blood of the guilt offering, and will put the priest on [the] lobe of [the] ear of the [one] cleansing himself, the right, and on [the] thumb of his hand, the right, and on [the] big toe of his foot, the right.
pieces: The priest is to take some of the guilt offering's blood and put it on the right earlobe of the person being cleansed, on their right thumb, and on the big toe of their right foot.

L.14: And the priest will take some of the blood of the guilt offering, and the priest will put [it] on the lobe of the right ear of the one being cleansed, and on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.

R.14: The priest must take some of the blood from the guilt offering. He must put it on the bottom of the person's right ear, on their right thumb and on the big toe of their right foot.

decisions.choice: ear, thumb and big toe: the same marks as at the priests' ordination
decisions.reason: Moses put the blood of the ordination ram on the same three places on Aaron and his sons (8:23-24; Exodus 29:20). Only these two rites use them. Here they mark the healed person's return to the holy community; the ear, hand and foot stand for the whole person, from head to foot.

decisions.choice: the right: the stronger, favored side
decisions.reason: The right hand and side are the place of strength and honor in Scripture (Genesis 48:13-14; Psalm 110:1).

records.source: וְלָקַ֥ח הַכֹּהֵ֖ן מִלֹּ֣ג הַשָּׁ֑מֶן וְיָצַ֛ק עַל־כַּ֥ף הַכֹּהֵ֖ן הַשְּׂמָאלִֽית׃
records.gloss: And will take the priest from [the] log of the oil, and he will pour on [the] palm of the priest, the left.
pieces: Next the priest is to take some of the log of oil and pour it into the palm of his own left hand.

L.15: And the priest will take some of the log of oil and pour [it] on the palm of the priest's left [hand].

R.15: Then the priest must pour some of the oil into his own left hand.

decisions.choice: the palm of the priest: his own palm
decisions.reason: "The priest" is named again, though he is the one acting, to make plain whose hand the oil is poured into: the officiating priest's own left hand, which then holds it while he uses his right finger (verse 16).

decisions.choice: his own
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "his own" for the Hebrew's "the priest's", which would sound like a second priest.

records.source: וְטָבַ֤ל הַכֹּהֵן֙ אֶת־אֶצְבָּע֣וֹ הַיְמָנִ֔ית מִן־הַשֶּׁ֕מֶן אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל־כַּפּ֖וֹ הַשְּׂמָאלִ֑ית וְהִזָּ֨ה מִן־הַשֶּׁ֧מֶן בְּאֶצְבָּע֛וֹ שֶׁ֥בַע פְּעָמִ֖ים לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

R.16: He must dip a finger of his right hand into the oil and sprinkle some of it seven times before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: sprinkle oil seven times before the LORD: toward the sanctuary
decisions.reason: Blood was sprinkled this way "before the LORD, in front of the veil" (4:6). This sprinkling of oil is unique to this rite; it seems to set the oil apart for God before it is put on the person, as anointing oil was sprinkled at the priests' ordination (8:11, 30).

decisions.choice: forefinger
decisions.reason: The finger used for sprinkling is the pointing finger. Literal keeps "finger".

records.source: וּמִיֶּ֨תֶר הַשֶּׁ֜מֶן אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־כַּפּ֗וֹ יִתֵּ֤ן הַכֹּהֵן֙ עַל־תְּנ֞וּךְ אֹ֤זֶן הַמִּטַּהֵר֙ הַיְמָנִ֔ית וְעַל־בֹּ֤הֶן יָדוֹ֙ הַיְמָנִ֔ית וְעַל־בֹּ֥הֶן רַגְל֖וֹ הַיְמָנִ֑ית עַ֖ל דַּ֥ם הָאָשָֽׁם׃

R.17: Then the priest must take some of the oil left in his hand. He must put it on the same places as the blood: the person's right ear, right thumb and right big toe.

decisions.choice: on the blood: on top of where the blood was put
decisions.reason: The oil goes on the same three places as the blood in verse 14. Verse 28 says "on the place of the blood".

decisions.choice: oil after blood: as at the priests' ordination
decisions.reason: Aaron and his sons were marked with blood and then sprinkled with oil (8:23-24, 30). Oil in Scripture marks someone set apart and honored (8:12; Psalm 23:5).

records.source: וְהַנּוֹתָ֗ר בַּשֶּׁ֨מֶן֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל־כַּ֣ף הַכֹּהֵ֔ן יִתֵּ֖ן עַל־רֹ֣אשׁ הַמִּטַּהֵ֑ר וְכִפֶּ֥ר עָלָ֛יו הַכֹּהֵ֖ן לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

L.18: And the rest of the oil that [is] on the priest's palm he will put on the head of the one being cleansed, and the priest will make atonement for him before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.18: He must put the rest of the oil from his hand on the person's head. In this way the priest will make atonement for them before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: make atonement for him: remove what keeps him from God
decisions.reason: On atonement see 1:4. Here it is made for uncleanness from disease, not only for sin (verse 19 says "from his uncleanness"). The whole rite, with the oil and the offerings, restores the person to God's presence.

decisions.choice: oil on the head
decisions.reason: Oil poured on the head marks Aaron's anointing as priest (8:12). Here the healed person receives the rest of the oil on their head, the last act with the oil.

records.source: וְעָשָׂ֤ה הַכֹּהֵן֙ אֶת־הַ֣חַטָּ֔את וְכִפֶּ֕ר עַל־הַמִּטַּהֵ֖ר מִטֻּמְאָת֑וֹ וְאַחַ֖ר יִשְׁחַ֥ט אֶת־הָעֹלָֽה׃
records.gloss: And will offer the priest the sin offering, and he will make atonement for the [one] cleansing himself from his uncleanness; and after he will slaughter the burnt offering.
pieces: The priest is then to offer the sin offering and make atonement for the person being cleansed from their uncleanness. After that he is to slaughter the burnt offering.

L.19: And the priest will offer the sin offering and make atonement for the one being cleansed from his uncleanness; and after [that] he will slaughter the burnt offering.

R.19: Next the priest must offer the sin offering. It will make atonement for the person and take away their uncleanness. After that the priest must kill the animal for the burnt offering.

decisions.choice: sin offering ... from his uncleanness: the offering purifies
decisions.reason: The sin offering is brought here not for a sin but for uncleanness, as after childbirth (12:6-8). This shows its sense of purification; see 4:3.

decisions.choice: and after: the order of the offerings
decisions.reason: Guilt offering, then sin offering, then burnt offering and grain offering (verse 20): the offerings that deal with wrong and uncleanness come before the offering wholly given to God.

decisions.choice: take away their uncleanness
decisions.reason: Readable says what making atonement "from" uncleanness does.

records.source: וְהֶעֱלָ֧ה הַכֹּהֵ֛ן אֶת־הָעֹלָ֥ה וְאֶת־הַמִּנְחָ֖ה הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חָה וְכִפֶּ֥ר עָלָ֛יו הַכֹּהֵ֖ן וְטָהֵֽר׃ס
records.gloss: And will offer up the priest the burnt offering and the grain offering on the altar, and will make atonement for him the priest, and he will be clean.
pieces: He is to offer up the burnt offering and the grain offering on the altar. So the priest will make atonement for them, and they will be clean.

L.20: And the priest will offer up the burnt offering and the grain offering on the altar, and the priest will make atonement for him, and he will be clean.

R.20: He must offer the burnt offering and the grain offering on the altar. In this way the priest will make atonement for the person, and they will be clean.

decisions.choice: he will be clean: the cleansing is complete
decisions.reason: This is the last of the three stages (verses 8, 9, 20). The person may now enter the sanctuary courts and take part in its holy meals.

decisions.choice: the grain offering: the flour of verse 10
decisions.reason: The three tenths of flour mixed with oil go with the animal offerings, as grain offerings go with burnt offerings in Numbers 15:4-9. On the grain offering see 2:1.

pieces: If they are poor and cannot afford this much, they are to take one male lamb as a guilt offering to be waved, to make atonement for them, with {{units:about 2 quarts|a tenth of an ephah}} of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering, and {{units:about a third of a quart|a log}} of oil,

L.21: And if he [is] poor and his hand cannot reach [so far], then he will take one male lamb [as] a guilt offering for waving, to make atonement for him, and one tenth [of an ephah] of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering, and a log of oil,

R.21: Some people are poor and cannot pay for all of this. A person like that must bring one male lamb for a guilt offering, which the priest will wave. It will make atonement for them. They must also bring {{units:about 2 quarts|a tenth of an ephah}} of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering, and {{units:about a third of a quart|a log}} of olive oil.

decisions.choice: his hand not reaching: he cannot afford it
decisions.reason: "His hand reaches" means a person has the means (5:7, 11; 12:8). The same phrase comes back in verses 22, 30-32.

decisions.choice: one male lamb as a guilt offering: the guilt offering is never reduced
decisions.reason: The poor person still brings a lamb for the guilt offering, with the full log of oil, and the whole rite with blood and oil (verses 24-29). Only the sin and burnt offerings are reduced to birds (verse 22), and the flour to one tenth.

decisions.choice: Some people are poor ... A person like that
decisions.reason: Readable turns the long condition into separate sentences. Balanced keeps one sentence running into verse 22.

records.heading: Cleansing for someone who is poor

records.source: וּשְׁתֵּ֣י תֹרִ֗ים א֤וֹ שְׁנֵי֙ בְּנֵ֣י יוֹנָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּשִּׂ֖יג יָד֑וֹ וְהָיָ֤ה אֶחָד֙ חַטָּ֔את וְהָאֶחָ֖ד עֹלָֽה׃

decisions.choice: turtledoves or young pigeons: the offering of those with little
decisions.reason: The same birds are allowed in 1:14, 5:7 and 12:8; Mary and Joseph brought them after Jesus' birth (Luke 2:24).

decisions.choice: which his hand reaches: whichever he can afford
decisions.reason: The clause may mean "whichever of the two kinds he can afford" or simply "as he can afford". Either way, it is the poor person's means that set the offering.

decisions.choice: the same as verse 12

L.34: "When you come into the land of Canaan, which I am giving to you as a possession, and I put a mark of scale disease in a house in the land of your possession,

R.34: "Someday you will go into the land of Canaan. I am giving it to you to be your own. While you are living there, I may put a patch of mold in one of your houses.

decisions.choice: a mark of scale disease in a house: a spreading growth on the walls, such as mold
decisions.reason: The word used for the skin disease in chapter 13 is also used for a growth in cloth or leather (13:47-59) and here in the walls of a house. It cannot be the same illness in walls and in skin; the word names a kind of blight that makes something unclean, whatever it grows on. Verse 37 describes greenish or reddish patches sunk into the wall that can spread (verses 39, 44). This fits a mold or fungus, or a mineral growth in damp stone; the text does not say which.

decisions.choice: and I put: God is the one who sends it
decisions.reason: The LORD says that he himself puts the mark in the house. The law does not say why; it treats the mark as a matter of uncleanness to be handled by the priest, not as a punishment of the owner.

decisions.choice: when you come into the land of Canaan: a law for life in the land
decisions.reason: Israel lived in tents in the wilderness. This law looks ahead to stone houses in Canaan, as do 18:3, 19:23, 23:10 and 25:2.

decisions.choice: a patch of mold
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "mold" for a growth in a house, as for cloth in 13:47, and "patch" for the mark. Literal keeps "mark of scale disease", the same words as for the skin, so a reader can see that the Hebrew uses one term for both.

decisions.choice: Someday ... While you are living there
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the long "when" clause into short sentences. Balanced keeps one sentence running into verse 35.

decisions.choice: like a mark: something that looks like one

R.36: The priest must tell the people to carry everything out of the house before he goes in to look at the mold. That way the things inside will not become unclean. Then the priest must go in and check the house.

decisions.choice: so that all in the house will not become unclean: uncleanness begins with the priest's ruling
decisions.reason: Until the priest sees the mark and rules, the house and its contents are not unclean. Clearing it first saves the household's goods; anything still inside when the house is pronounced unclean would be unclean too, and clay pots would have to be broken (11:33; 15:12).

decisions.choice: empty the house: clear everything out of it
decisions.reason: The verb means to turn aside or clear away, here to clear a house of its contents (compare Genesis 24:31, "I have prepared the house").

decisions.choice: lower than the wall: like a mark deeper than the skin
decisions.reason: This matches the sign of real disease in a person, a mark that looks "deeper than the skin" (13:3).

decisions.choice: has been healed: the mark is gone

R.49: To make the house clean, he must get two birds, some cedar wood, some red yarn and a hyssop plant.

decisions.choice: to purify: to cleanse from what defiles
decisions.reason: The verb is formed from the word for sin and the sin offering, and means to take sin or uncleanness away (8:15; Numbers 19:19; Psalm 51:9). A house has no sin; the sense is purification.

decisions.choice: two birds, cedar wood, scarlet yarn and hyssop: as in verse 4
decisions.reason: The house is cleansed with the same rite as the person (verses 4-7). See verse 4. There are no animal offerings for the house.

R.51: Then he must take the cedar wood, the hyssop, the red yarn and the live bird. He must dip all of them in the blood of the dead bird and the fresh water. He must sprinkle the house seven times.

decisions.reason: This makes plain what verse 6 implied: the blood and the water are together in the pot.

decisions.choice: sprinkle on the house seven times
decisions.reason: The same sprinkling as on the person (verse 7).

pieces: So he will purify the house with the bird's blood, the fresh water, the live bird, the cedar wood, the hyssop and the scarlet yarn.

L.52: And he will purify the house with the blood of the bird and with the living water and with the living bird and with the cedar wood and with the hyssop and with the scarlet yarn.

R.52: This is how he will make the house clean. He will use the bird's blood, the fresh water, the live bird, the cedar wood, the hyssop and the red yarn.

decisions.choice: with ... with ... with: every part of the rite has its share
decisions.reason: The verse names each of the six things in turn, each with its own "with", to stress that together they purify the house.

pieces: He is to set the live bird free outside the town in the open country. So he will make atonement for the house, and it will be clean.

L.53: And he will let the living bird go outside the city over the face of the field, and he will make atonement for the house, and it will be clean.

R.53: Then he must let the live bird fly away outside the town into the open fields. In this way he will make atonement for the house, and it will be clean.

decisions.choice: make atonement for the house: cleansing a thing, not forgiving a sin
decisions.reason: Atonement can be made for things as well as people: for the altar (8:15; 16:18) and the sanctuary (16:16). Here it means that the house's uncleanness is taken away and it can be lived in again.

decisions.choice: the living bird set free: as in verse 7
decisions.reason: See verse 7. For the house the bird is released outside the town, away from where people live.

L.54: This [is] the law for every mark of scale disease, and for the scall,

decisions.choice: this is the law: a summary of chapters 13 and 14
decisions.reason: Verses 54-57 are one sentence that sums up both chapters. It names the cases the two chapters cover: marks on the skin, on the head and beard, in cloth and in a house, and the signs first named in 13:2.

decisions.choice: the scall: an itching, scaly patch where the hair grows
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for a mark on the head or beard in 13:30-37. It comes from a verb meaning to tear or pull out, perhaps from the scratching or the loss of hair it causes.

pieces: for mold in clothing and in a house,

R.55: and for mold in clothing or in a house.

decisions.choice: the garment and the house: 13:47-59 and 14:34-53
decisions.reason: The one word for the disease covers both cases; see 13:47 and verse 34.

decisions.choice: mold
decisions.reason: As in verse 34, Balanced and Readable say "mold" for the growth in cloth or a house. Literal keeps "scale disease".

decisions.choice: swelling, scab and bright spot: the signs of 13:2
decisions.reason: These are the three marks on the skin with which chapter 13 begins (13:2). On their meanings see the notes there.

pieces: for teaching which day a thing is unclean and which day it is clean. This is the law for serious skin disease and mold."

decisions.reason: "On the day of" means "when". The purpose of these laws is to let the priests rule rightly between unclean and clean, which is their task (10:10-11; Ezekiel 44:23).

decisions.reason: The summary ends as verse 32 and 13:59 do, with the word "law" and the name of the disease that covers every case.

decisions.choice: serious skin disease and mold
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has one word for the disease in people, cloth and houses. Balanced and Readable name both, so as not to leave out the cases of verses 34-55. Literal keeps the single term.
